Plugin.Name: Komari Agent
Plugin.Description: Run the Komari monitoring agent on Unraid as a managed service.
Plugin.Overview:
The Komari agent reports CPU, memory, disk, network throughput, load and uptime to a Komari status panel over a WebSocket connection.
The agent is a long running daemon, and Unraid has none of what a daemon needs: no systemd, no persistent /usr, no log rotation for a new service. This plugin supplies that layer.
[b]Features:[/b] - Starts on boot and stops cleanly on shutdown, through an rc script at /etc/rc.d/rc.komari-agent. - A supervisor loop restarts the agent when it crashes. - The binary is cached on the flash device and re-installed on every boot, because /usr is an overlay filesystem. - Log rotation for /var/log/komari-agent.log, which lives on a tmpfs. - A Settings page edits the configuration, restarts the agent and shows live status, including a panel connectivity probe. - Traffic counters are persisted on flash, so they survive a reboot.
[b]Safe defaults:[/b] - Panel-issued remote control (Web SSH and RCE) is disabled by default. - The agent's built-in self-update is disabled by default, because the overlay filesystem would discard the result and it would bypass the pinned checksum. - The agent token is passed through the environment only, never on a command line.
[b]Requirements:[/b] - Unraid 7.0 or newer, x86_64 - An existing Komari panel and an agent token issued by it
The upstream binary is redistributed unmodified and is verified against a pinned SHA256 on every build.
